docs.title: qemu-minimal
docs.text:
Documentation and live CI output qemu-minimal Pages

A documentation-first landing page for the published VM reports, compose stacks, and continuously refreshed benchmark snapshots that qemu-minimal exposes through GitHub Pages.

Browse report lanes Performance trends Documentation Tracked performance

Green is within 5% of the mean of the last five distinct readings, amber within 20%, red below that.

Published reports

Single VM, rocjitsu, rocm-ernic, and hipFile fio outputs stay live on the site and are refreshed by CI. The badge above carries the last date on which every lane published a fresh passing report.

Publishing model

The site is assembled on gh-pages from named workflow artifacts plus repository-owned documentation content.

Reports Inspect the current guests

Every report comes from a real CI boot — the published output reflects the guest CI actually produced, not static documentation.

rocjitsu and hipFile artifacts feed a retained history on gh-pages, producing the latest badges and a trend page over time.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
Reports What is live

Seven CI lanes publish guest inspection pages: single-VM, rocjitsu, ernic, lmcache, quickstart, MI355X, and hipFile fio. Each page is regenerated from the latest artifact and linked from the report index.

Performance What is retained

Benchmark lanes expose numeric badge JSON. Those snapshots accumulate in a history file on gh-pages so the performance page shows trends rather than only the latest reading.

Publishing How it fits together

The Pages publisher fetches each lane's latest artifact by name and assembles them into one site. No lane can overwrite another's content.

docs.title: Site sections
docs.text: Section Purpose Home Landing page with badges, site summary, and entry points. Documentation High-level explanation of the published site and its moving parts. Reports Directory of the live CI-generated report pages. Publishing flow How workflow artifacts become the published site and how trend history is retained. Performance trends Generated benchmark history, latest badges, and recent-run tables.

docs.title: Report-producing lanes
docs.text: Workflow Published path Notes report-for-vm-basic /1vm/ General single-VM guest inspection. report-for-vm-rocjitsu /rocjitsu/ rocjitsu VM report with GEMM and hipFile benchmark output. report-for-vm-ernic /ernic/ and /ernic/vm2/ ernic stack reports for VM 1 and VM 2. report-for-hipfile-fio /hipfile-fio/ fio libhipfile benchmark report. report-for-lmcache /lmcache/ LMCache L1 P2P between two guests, with the ernic RDMA byte counters. report-for-quickstart /quickstart/ The README's Quick Start, run end to end. report-for-mi355x /mi355x/ An MI355X-shaped PCIe tree, as the guest enumerates it.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The site is built from docs/ using MkDocs Material and pushed as pre-built HTML to the gh-pages branch.
  • Live report artifacts remain the source of truth for guest state.
  • Performance history is stored only on gh-pages; it is not committed on main.

docs.title: Site assembly
docs.text:
The published site is built from two sources:

  1. Repository-owned Pages content under docs/.
  2. The latest unexpired report artifacts uploaded by the report workflows.

The qemu-minimal-publish-pages.yml workflow fetches each report artifact by name into the docs/ tree, runs mkdocs build to produce site/, and pushes the built HTML to the gh-pages branch.

docs.title: Performance tracking flow
docs.text: The rocjitsu and hipFile fio artifacts expose metric badge JSON. The publisher reads those badges, appends a new record when metrics change, and regenerates the performance page and badge JSON from a history file on gh-pages. That keeps main free of CI-written history while retaining trends over time.

docs.title: Adding another report lane
docs.text:
1. Upload lane output under its own stable artifact name.
  2. Fetch that artifact into docs/<dest>/ in qemu-minimal-publish-pages.yml.
  3. Add the lane's workflow name: to the workflow_run trigger list — omit this and the lane publishes nothing until another lane finishes.
  4. Add the lane to the report index and, if it exposes numeric badges, to the performance renderer.
  5. Add a status badge to the README — omit this and the lane is invisible on the report page.

docs.title: Failure model
docs.text:
• Missing artifacts leave the last published lane output in place.
  • Retried Pages publishes rebuild from the latest gh-pages tip before pushing.
  • Performance history is regenerated from the seeded gh-pages record, so a re-run does not truncate the trend page to one point.

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
Single guest Single VM report

One gen-vm guest with NVMe attached, built and inspected on a GitHub-hosted runner.

GPU guest rocjitsu report

rocjitsu guest inspection plus the current GEMM and hipFile benchmark outputs.

Two guests ernic report

The ernic stack, with VM 1 at the top-level page and VM 2 nested underneath.

Two guests lmcache report

LMCache L1 P2P between two guests: whether the KV bytes crossed the ernic as RDMA rather than falling back to TCP.

Two guests quickstart report

The README's Quick Start, run daily: qemu-tool quick-start brings up two guests from the published image, each with a GPU, an NVMe and an RDMA NIC, plus Prometheus and Grafana, with a GPU test and an inter-guest RDMA test.

Node shape MI355X node report

An MI355X-shaped PCIe tree: 8 GPUs, 8 RDMA NICs and 8 switches in one guest, one NIC and one GPU below each switch, with the tree the guest actually enumerates.

fio lane hipFile fio report

The fio libhipfile benchmark lane, published independently from the rocjitsu report.

DKMS bake Ernic SRQ+P4 bake report

Boots the published ernic-rocjitsu qcow2 and bakes the SRQ+P4 ionic DKMS stack in; verifies ernic_p4.ko is present and loadable.

docs.title: Publishing model
docs.text: Each lane uploads a named artifact; the Pages publisher assembles the latest artifact from every lane so one run cannot overwrite another's content. The site stays complete even when a lane has not run for days.

docs.title: hipFile fio Benchmark
docs.text:
Metric Value fio libhipfile read throughput 70.4 MB/s

This is fio's own libhipfile ioengine reading from the guest NVMe straight into VRAM, rather than the hand-written benchmark the rocjitsu report uses. fio is built in the guest from a pinned master commit, because the engine is not in any fio release tag. Same caveat as the other lanes: the GPU is emulated over vfio-user, so watch the trend between runs rather than the absolute number.

docs.title: MI355X-shaped node report
docs.text:
One guest with 8 GPUs, 8 emulated RDMA NICs and 8 PCIe switches -- one NIC and one GPU below each switch, each switch on its own root port. Every other stack in this repo hangs one NIC and one GPU flat off the root complex, so this is the only lane that exercises software reading a realistic PCIe tree.

  • Guest image: 20261021.g0f1f43f-vm.resolute-ernic-rocjitsu-qm.b4eb552-qcow2
  • Fleet size: 1 VM (the lab stack is 4; a runner fits one)
  • Addressed NICs: 1 of 8. All 8 RDMA devices come up, but 99-rocm-ernic.rules names the Ethernet interface rocm-ernic%n and %n is 0 for every one of them, so a single NIC wins that name and the other seven keep kernel names. Only the named one carries an address.
  • Generated: 2026-11-02 22:34 UTC · Commit: unknown · Status: pass

docs.title: Performance trends
docs.text: This page is generated during the Pages publish from retained benchmark history on gh-pages, using the latest rocjitsu and hipFile fio report artifacts as inputs. It mirrors the same basic model used by the ROCm/rocm-ernic site: badges for the latest published numbers, a durable history file, and a trend page regenerated as new CI data lands.

docs.title: Latest published snapshot
docs.text:
Generated from fad1f5e8 at 2026-11-12 20:17 UTC.

Badge colour is health, not branding. Each latest reading is compared against the mean of the previous 5 distinct readings — consecutive republishes of an unchanged number are collapsed first, because a publish is triggered by any report lane finishing and re-records the other lanes' last artifacts untouched. Green is at or above 95% of that baseline, amber down to 80%, red below it, and blue means there is not yet a second distinct reading to compare against. The band is wide on purpose: these benchmarks run against an emulated GPU over vfio-user and swing hard between runs.

docs.text:
A report counts as green when it carries a pass status stamp and was generated within 36 hours of the publish. Both are needed: a lane that fails uploads no artifact at all, so its previous report stays on the branch and would otherwise keep reading pass indefinitely. The badge above shows the last date on which all 7 reports were green at once — amber once that date is no longer today.
